LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 8.3.1 WORD CLASSES

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why do we shorten words like cannot to can’t?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. form appropriate contracted forms of verbs in varied texts,
2. use positive and negative statements in sentences,
3. realise the importance of correct sentence structures in communication. The learner is guided to: audio or written text, negative or positive statements in small groups then display the work on a chart, use them in sentences correctly, negative statements and vice versa, both positive and negative answers, contracted forms of verbs, online resources on contracted verbs. SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes.
2. Explain Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes.
4. Show that you can: form appropriate contracted forms of verbs in varied texts,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why do we shorten words like cannot to can’t?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.
